issues.description:
Method return type mismatch for Stock.take(String):
- Problem statement (UML) declares Stock.take(String): int (uses -1 to indicate failure).
- Solution repository implements Stock.take(String) returning int and SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() calls stock.take(x) and compares the result to -1.
- Template repository implements Stock.take(String) returning boolean. This mismatch (boolean vs int) will cause compilation errors or incorrect usage for students (calls expecting an int cannot compile against a boolean-returning method) and confuses the intended contract (should return -1 on failure and remaining quantity on success).
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template to match the problem statement and solution: change the signature of Stock.take(String) from returning boolean to returning int. Implement the method so it returns -1 to indicate failure (ingredient not found or quantity < 1) and returns the remaining quantity (or new quantity) on success, consistent with the solution. Ensure any callers (including SealSaloon.checkOrderReady) use the int return convention. This preserves the intended exercise contract and prevents compile-time mismatches.
